on_the_swamp.blurb: The Swamp is one of Ontario's newer crags, in the south of the province. It is mostly sport, with several moderate trad lines, and grades run from about 5.6 to 5.13, with the bulk between 5.10 and 5.12 and a fair number of moderates. The cliff faces south and has both sun and shade, with plenty of tree cover, and the southern exposure suits cooler spring and fall days. Grading may feel lenient on some routes. The largest sectors are Big Boy Wall, The Islands, The Wall of Shadows, The Last Stand Wall and Yellow Card Wall.

tx_main_dome.blurb: Main Dome is the largest single feature at Enchanted Rock State Natural Area near Llano, Texas, and holds the park's largest concentration of routes. The park's climbing is on granite domes and boulders, mainly traditional, with bolted lines that can be sporty. Bouldering, trad and some sport are all here, with most problems easy and routes mostly from 5.8 to 5.11. The Backside has the longest climbs in the park, mostly bolted slabs, with The Shield, News Wall and Devil's Slide among its walls. Echo Canyon offers single-pitch climbing, and a small bouldering area sits on the front side.

ut_ferguson_canyon.blurb: Ferguson Canyon is a small canyon just south of Big Cottonwood Canyon in the Central Wasatch, near Salt Lake City. Several small crags sit on north-facing walls shaded by large trees, which makes it a summer refuge. The climbing is mostly trad with a good share of sport and a little top-rope, on quartz monzonite that is solid and blocky with horizontal cracks, though it can get slick on busy routes. Grades run from 5.4 to 5.12, mostly 5.9 to 5.11, and routes are mostly short. The Watchtower and The Cathedral hold the most climbs, followed by Goldenfingers Wall.

ca_backcountry_bouldering.blurb: Backcountry Bouldering covers boulders scattered through the forest above Idyllwild in the San Jacinto Mountains. The problems are hard to locate and reaching them means long hikes on various trails. It is mostly bouldering, mostly V0 to V4, with a few trad lines. The range's rock is granite, ranging from very smooth to quite gritty, and most of the mountains sit above 6,000 feet, making them mainly a spring-through-fall destination. Sub-areas include Laws Caramba Trail, Red Tahquitz, Seven Pines and Willow Creek Trail.

il_a_north_canyon.blurb: North Canyon is the northernmost section of Jackson Falls in the Shawnee National Forest of southern Illinois, running from Mr. Jimmy through Railroad Rock. The canyon's cliffs are sandstone. Climbing here is mainly sport, with some trad and a little bouldering, and grades run from about 5.6 to 5.13, with the bulk between 5.10 and 5.12. Big Star Wall, Railroad Rock Cliffline and Hobo Cave are among the larger sub-areas, and Railroad Rock is described as mostly shady and occasionally damp. At Jackson Falls generally, September through December is described as the most pleasant weather, with spring also good but wetter.
